USMLE-style practice · Clinical medicine

Multiple ectopic atrial foci

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 55-year-old has intermittent premature atrial beats on a long rhythm strip. The premature P waves have two clearly different shapes, while the usual sinus P waves remain unchanged. What does this finding most directly suggest?

  1. A single ventricular focus for all beats
  2. Permanent absence of sinus-node activity
  3. A single fixed AV conduction delay
  4. Complete ventricular standstill
  5. More than one ectopic atrial focus
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

More than one ectopic atrial focus

Different premature P-wave morphologies suggest different atrial activation origins.

Understanding the options

More than one ectopic atrial focus
Different premature P-wave morphologies suggest different atrial activation origins.
A single ventricular focus for all beats
The beats begin with ectopic P waves, indicating atrial rather than ventricular origin.
Permanent absence of sinus-node activity
Normal sinus beats remain present.
A single fixed AV conduction delay
Conduction delay alone does not create distinct ectopic atrial activation contours.
Complete ventricular standstill
Ventricular responses are present.
